name: HP LaserJet M110w

model_variants.this_model: HP LaserJet M110w, product number 7MD66F (#B19 Europe/Middle East, 220-240 V; #BGJ USA, 110-127 V). The Israeli shops sell 7MD66F.
model_variants.m110we: HP LaserJet M110we = 7MD66E, the HP+ version of the same printer (same body, same size). Differences are account/firmware/service only, see hp_plus.
model_variants.family: HP LaserJet M109-M112 series (M110w/M110we/M111w/M112w share the body)

hp_plus.m110we: M110we (7MD66E) is the HP+ version: needs an HP account and a permanent internet connection, and works only with original HP toner for the life of the printer; in return it adds an extra year of HP warranty and an Instant Ink trial (6 months in the US). The plain M110w (7MD66F, sold in Israel) has none of these requirements (1-year warranty) but is still 'dynamic security enabled': cartridges need an HP chip (new or reused). Same body and size.
hp_plus.israel: All Israeli listings found (zap.co.il, Kravitz, Misradia) are the M110w 7MD66F; no M110we offered in Israel.

closed.includes: HP 'minimum dimensions': input tray door closed, output extension pushed in. The 189 mm depth is the whole body, back face to front door; nothing on the back sticks out except the plugged-in cables. Some HP sheets round the height to 158 mm (M110we product sheet); the user guide, the EMEA datasheet and HP's 'Built to Fit' image say 159 mm.

max.what: HP 'maximum dimensions'. The height 280 mm is with the top cover (toner door, hinged at the back) raised, which is only needed to change toner. The user guide's 'printer fully open' table gives D 329.6 mm, H 280.1 mm.

weight_kg.what: printer with starter cartridge (user guide: 3.7 kg with cartridges; M110we sheet: ~3.79 kg)

duplex_note: HP lists 'Duplex printing: None' (no automatic duplex); the user guide describes printing on both sides by re-loading the printed stack by hand.

connectivity.detail: 1 Hi-Speed USB 2.0 (device, USB-B); Wi-Fi 802.11b/g/n 2.4 GHz only; Wi-Fi Direct; Bluetooth LE used for setup. No Ethernet port.

paper.manual_feed: none (envelopes and labels go in the same front tray)
paper.sizes: A4, A5, A6, envelopes C5/DL, custom; 65-120 g/m2

display: No screen: 3 LEDs (Attention, Ready, Wireless) and 3 buttons (Power, Cancel, Wireless)

toner.region_note: Israel and Europe use HP 142A (W1420A); the US/Asia-Pacific version uses HP 141A (W1410A), also ~950 pages. Cartridge and drum are one unit (no separate drum).

in_the_box.items: Printer, power cord (C13), starter toner cartridge (~300 pages), setup poster, reference guide, warranty guide, flyer. No USB cable. No CD (software is downloaded).
in_the_box.region: Europe/Middle East datasheet (7MD66F, 220-240 V); Israeli shops confirm 'comes without a USB cable'
in_the_box.notes: Kravitz's Israeli listing claims a 700-page starter toner; HP's own datasheets say 300 pages. Warranty in Israel: 1 year through the official importers (Techno Retzef / C-Data).

ils.where: Kravitz (official importer stock), cheapest of 37 shops on zap.co.il

usd.note: Online elsewhere: Staples $168.90, Office Depot $169.00, Best Buy $169.99 (M110w 7MD66F#BGJ)

power.type: C13 (IEC C14 inlet on the printer)
power.position: about 31.3 cm from the left edge seen from behind (3.3 cm from the right edge), centre 2.9 cm above the bottom; inlet turned 90 deg

data.position: about 31.9 cm from the left edge seen from behind (2.7 cm from the right edge), centre 9.9 cm above the bottom
data.note: in a corner pocket (about 3.4 cm wide, 5 cm tall, 2.5 cm deep, open to the back and to the left side); a USB-B plug is about 3 cm long, so it ends about 0.5 cm behind the back and only its strain relief sticks out

cable_space.why: The power inlet sits flush on a flat back, so the C13 plug (about 3.4 cm) plus its strain relief and the bent cable add about 6.8 cm behind the printer (3D model build: cables reach 6.8 cm); the USB plug is mostly hidden in its 2.5 cm corner pocket and needs only about 2.6 cm. The power plug sets the gap.

notes: The smallest printer in this comparison: 34.6 x 18.9 x 15.9 cm closed, so it fits the 24.5 cm shelf with room for the cables. To print, the front door folds down into the paper tray and sticks out about 14 cm in front (HP: about 33-36 cm total depth in use), and the output extension slides out over it. Paper is loaded only in that front tray; nothing opens at the back. Wi-Fi is 2.4 GHz only.
